prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a partition wall with three vertical glass door panels in front of the camera wearer in frames 1 to 3 (roughly 1 to 2 metres away, with the left wall coming within arm's reach at under 0.8 metres in frame 3), followed by the camera wearer turning right past a close wall/doorway in frame 4 (about 0.5 to 1 metre away) to face an open doorway and right-hand wall in frame 5. Through the glass panels in frames 1 to 3, an interior room with a white chair on the lower left (about 2.5 to 3.5 metres away) and deeper background spaces (4 to 6+ metres away) are visible, while in frame 5 a standing person appears in the doorway roughly 2.5 to 3 metres ahead to the left of a nearby right-hand wall (under 1 metre away). As the camera wearer approaches the left wall in frame 3 and turns right across frames 4 and 5, the bright foreground wall shifts from the left side of the view to the right side, placing the adjacent wall within arm's reach of the wearer while the standing person in frame 5 remains well beyond reach. The depth map clearly separates the near structural frames, walls, and taped paper sign on the middle glass panel from the recessed room interior, which is harder to judge in RGB due to reflections on the glass. However, the map is unreliable on the glass panes themselves—treating parts of the reflective/transparent surfaces as dark, distant voids while faintly bleeding the taped paper's depth—and it loses almost all furniture and person detail inside the room in frames 1 to 4.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map detects almost nothing of the scene layout across the five frames, failing to segment the glass doors, walls, armchairs, and background furniture visible in the RGB strip. It only produces four isolated masks: a partial 'person' mask at the bottom-center of frame 2 (roughly 2.5 to 3 metres away behind the glass door), a misclassified 'toilet' mask on the small white chair at the lower-left inside the room in frame 3 (about 2.5 to 3 metres away), a truncated 'person' mask on the far right edge of frame 4 (about 2 to 2.5 metres away, heavily occluded by the frame boundary), and a 'person' mask with a small adjacent 'car' false positive at the bottom-left in frame 5 (about 2.5 to 3 metres away in the doorway). In frame 5, the segmented standing person is positioned to the left of the foreground wall, facing right in profile and not looking toward the camera wearer, with their lower legs cropped out at the bottom of the frame and a held object near their waist within their own arm's reach. While the frame 5 silhouette clearly isolates the standing person's upper body and profile orientation against the bright doorway background, nothing in the segmented masks is within arm's reach of the camera wearer. Overall, the segmentation map is highly unreliable, missing the seated/crouching person inside the room in frames 1 and 3, missing all architectural structures and lounge furniture, and mislabelling indoor chairs and floor items as 'toilet' and 'car'.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely blank in frames 1, 2, and 4, detecting a yellow body skeleton only for the person inside the room behind the glass door in frame 3 (roughly 3 to 3.5 metres away, to the left of the central door mullions) and for the standing person in the doorway in frame 5 (roughly 2.5 to 3 metres away, to the left of the foreground wall). In frame 3, the skeleton shows a person in a crouched or seated posture facing rightward in profile and looking away from the camera wearer, with both knees bent and arms angled downward within their own reach of the floor/chair area; this clearly reveals a full human body posture inside the dimly lit room that is heavily obscured by glass reflections and dark clothing in the RGB image. In frame 5, as the camera wearer has turned right toward the open doorway, the skeleton shows an upright torso and head facing right (roughly perpendicular to the camera wearer's line of sight) with the right arm bent forward at the elbow and the legs below the hips cut off by the bottom frame edge. No magenta hand skeletons are detected in any frame, and neither detected person is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or near the other person across the scene transition. The pose map is unreliable where glass reflections and dim lighting cause it to miss the person inside the room in frames 1 and 2, and where motion blur and frame boundary truncation cause it to miss the partially visible person at the right edge of frame 4 and the lower limbs and hands in frame 5.
